title: Certificates of Deposit: Withdrawals Before Maturity, Owner Consent and Kinds of Withdrawal
content:
Money placed in the bank's Certificates of Deposit is committed until maturity. This page governs any withdrawal from a certificate before its maturity date: whose decision it is, which certificates can release principal early, and how the bank classifies the withdrawal, which in turn decides whether a penalty applies.

## The owner decides

Withdrawing before maturity is solely the owner's decision. The agent records an early withdrawal request on the certificate with the status of awaiting the customer's confirmation, and no money leaves the certificate unless and until the owner confirms that request.

## Only an active certificate releases principal early

No principal leaves a certificate ahead of its maturity date unless the bank's record shows the certificate in active status.

## Classifying the withdrawal

The bank assigns each early withdrawal exactly one kind, testing the descriptions below in the sequence shown; the earliest description that fits decides the kind.

| Sequence | Kind | When it fits | Penalty |
|---|---|---|---|
| A | Withdrawal of credited interest | The sum taken does not exceed the interest credited to the certificate during the current term, meaning interest compounded into it since the term start date less any credited interest already withdrawn in that term | None, on a tier where credited interest may be withdrawn free of penalty |
| B | Death or incompetence waiver | The owner has died or been adjudicated incompetent by a court, as confirmed by the bank's estate services | None, on a tier offering the waiver |
| C | Penalty-free withdrawal | A full withdrawal on a tier offering penalty-free withdrawal after a waiting period, taken once that period has passed | None |
| D | Early full or early partial withdrawal | Any other withdrawal before maturity | A penalty is charged |

| Tier | Credited interest withdrawable free of penalty | Death or incompetence waiver | Penalty-free full withdrawal after |
|---|---|---|---|
| 6-Month Certificate | No | Yes | not offered |
| 11-Month No-Penalty Certificate | Yes | Yes | 6 calendar days after funding |
| 12-Month Certificate | Yes | Yes | not offered |
| 18-Month Bump-Up Certificate | Yes | Yes | not offered |
| 36-Month Certificate | Yes | Yes | not offered |
| 60-Month Certificate | Yes | Yes | not offered |

## The penalty-free waiting period

A penalty-free withdrawal is available only after the tier's waiting period, in calendar days, has fully passed since the certificate was funded. The clock runs from the term start date on the certificate record, which is the day the opening deposit posted. Day 1 of the count is the calendar day following the term start date. The withdrawal qualifies on the date that is the waiting period plus one day after the term start date, and on any later date; the date exactly the waiting period after the term start date does not yet qualify.

## Boundary cases (hypothetical dates, 11-Month No-Penalty Certificate)

| Term start date | Withdrawal date | Day count | Penalty-free? |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 May | 7 May | day 6 | No; the waiting days have not fully passed |
| 1 May | 8 May | day 7 | Yes, for a full withdrawal |
| 1 May | 20 May | day 19 | Yes, for a full withdrawal |

## Points of judgement

**The owner of an active 12-Month Certificate asks, before maturity, for a sum no larger than the interest credited in the current term (hypothetical).** Description A fits, and that tier lets credited interest out free of penalty, so no penalty is charged.
